primary_issue: Camera framing/subject scale is wrong: the mug is tiny and distant, so the shot does not read as a studio product closeup on a concrete countertop.
issues: Mug is extremely small/distant in frame; composition does not function as a product closeup.
Countertop does not convincingly read as concrete (surface looks flat/featureless).
Lighting/background are washed out with low contrast; white mug blends into the white background (poor separation).
Backdrop/floor setup shows slab/plane boundaries/gradients instead of a clean seamless white studio background.
Mug material/shape definition is weak (insufficient highlights/edge definition for ceramic).
suggestions: (setup_camera, modify_code) Move camera much closer and lower to a product-shot angle; reframe so the mug occupies ~25–40% of the image. If focal length/FOV is very wide, increase focal length to reduce “distant” feel.

(setup_lighting, modify_code) Add clearer key/fill/rim separation: stronger directional key + subtle rim to outline the mug against white; slightly increase shadow definition to anchor the mug to the counter.

(setup_materials, modify_code) Replace/upgrade the countertop shader to a proper concrete look (roughness variation + micro-bump + subtle speckling). Use higher-frequency detail so it reads at close range.
(setup_scene, modify_code) Use a seamless cyclorama (curved infinity wall) to eliminate visible floor/wall plane transitions; keep background uniformly clean.
(bake_and_render / lookdev, modify_params) Reduce background brightness: Line 206 bg Strength 0.9 → ~0.2–0.5 so the mug doesn’t disappear into the background.

(lookdev, modify_params) Increase overall contrast via color management: Line 140 settings.look = None → try a Filmic contrast look (e.g., “Medium High Contrast”) to restore separation without clipping.

(setup_materials, modify_params) If the current procedural texture is driving surface detail, adjust scale/detail to make microstructure visible: Line 595 tex Scale 1.0 → ~3–8; Line 596 tex Detail 10.0 → ~2–6 (avoid noisy/overly sharp speckle).
vision_assessment: The image is dominated by a bright, nearly featureless white environment. A small mug silhouette is visible near the top-center, but it is far away and lacks the prominence expected from a studio product closeup. The countertop surface does not read as concrete due to minimal visible texture/roughness variation, and the backdrop/floor shows slab-like boundaries/gradients rather than a clean seamless white background. Lighting is flat and over-bright, causing the white mug to blend into the background with weak edge highlights and poor subject separation.
